members.title: Badenoch says using amputee athletes to justify cutting disability benefits was ‘message of hope’ – UK politics live
members.lead: PM has asked Badenoch to withdraw her suggestion that benefits should be cut because ‘double amputees run marathons’ These are from my colleague Peter Walker, who was at the Tory event where James Cleverly was named as the party’s candidate for London mayor. Peter posted this before the result was announced. Khan (who may or may not stand a 4th time) has thus far faced a dilettante who decided to campaign on a racist platform (Zack Goldsmith) and two oddballs in Shaun Bailey and then Susan Hall. Not even he can be lucky yet again Interesting that [the Conservatives] did not say how many votes were cast, just the percentage - which perhaps indicates it was not a huge number Cleverly’s speech is mainly an attack on Labour and Khan, which is likely to be a theme for his campaign: “Burnham can’t stand London and Khan stand up to Burnham.” Also a pitch about building houses and cutting crime, and boosting transport. Cleverly says he would “end Khan’s war on motorists”, which is a sign he might lean into the anti-cycling and walking rhetoric which the London Tories have a habit of espousing. Expect talk about LTNs and 20mph zones. In the media Q&A Cleverly is pinned down on whether he backs the Tory party line on wanting to leave the ECHR and opposes net zero. He confirms he does (as he has to). Such things will be ready ammunition for Labour. Cleverly says of Andy Burnham, “His residual behaviour is to be anti-London”. This will very much be a theme of his campaign, it seems. Not sure how resonant a “poor London!” message will be even in London People are leaving London, or not choosing to come here in the first place, businesses, job creators, families leaving London, and by the time of the election in 2028, Khan will have been mayor for 12 years, and those two things are related. The problems London faces are the symptoms. Khan is the cause. Continue reading...

members.title: Tories select James Cleverly as candidate for London mayor
members.lead: Former home secretary wins 86% support in a membership vote to stand in May 2028 James Cleverly has been chosen by the Conservatives as their candidate in the next London mayoral election and says he will stand up to “anti-London” Andy Burnham. Cleverly, who stood down as shadow communities secretary in August to focus on his mayoral ambitions, was overwhelmingly chosen in a vote of London Tory members from a three-strong shortlist, winning 86% of the ballot.
